subject: Price bridge & implementation acceptance
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Maria Gonzales <maria@cloudbridge.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-07-12T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Price bridge & implementation acceptance

Hi Maria —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Two quick notes to capture what we discussed and to make the ask explicit so we can move to a signed SOW:

1) Pricing alignment: CloudBridge has asked for a unit-price parity with your incumbent for the first 12 months. You mentioned target effective discounting to match their blended runtime cost.

2) Implementation acceptance: your engineering team needs a two-week acceptance window after go-live (production traffic) to confirm latency and KV cache behavior before the final milestone payment.

Our proposed path (what I can commit to now):
- 6-month price bridge to match incumbent effective rate on raw token spend (details in a follow-up table).
- A one-time onboarding credit to cover migration egress + two onboarding engineers for up to 40 hours.
- A staged acceptance: pilot → canary → production with a two-week acceptance window post-prod. If acceptance tests fail on latency SLOs we will: 1) roll back the rollout plan; 2) provide targeted runtime tuning and an additional week of engineering support at no charge.

Can you confirm these are acceptable high-level terms? If yes, we’ll send a short amendment + SOW to legal and start scheduling the onboarding kickoff for July 21.

Thanks — Jordan

--
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachment stubs: pricing-bridge-summary.pdf (table), kickoff-checklist.md
From: Maria Gonzales <maria@cloudbridge.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Daniel Park <daniel.park@cloudbridge.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-07-12T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Price bridge & implementation acceptance

Jordan —

Appreciate the recap. Quick reactions from our side after reviewing with finance and infra:

- Pricing: parity on raw token spend for 6 months is a good start but finance needs a clear definition of "effective rate" (token definition, rounding, and peak vs baseline). Can you send the calculation example showing the incumbent invoice -> Redwood equivalent?

- Onboarding credit: good. Please specify whether the credit is refundable or applied as a dollar credit against the first two invoices.

- Acceptance window: two weeks is standard; our infra lead asked that you include a documented list of acceptance tests (latency p95, tail latency, KV cache cold-start behavior under 10% traffic). We also want an explicit escalation path if acceptance fails (contact, SLA to remediate).

We’re broadly aligned but need those specifics before procurement will sign. Also — timeline: July 21 kickoff is tight for our SSO and network setup. Can we aim for July 28 (gives our security team a week)?

Thanks,
Maria

--
Maria Gonzales
Head of Platform, CloudBridge, Inc.
maria@cloudbridge.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Maria Gonzales <maria@cloudbridge.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-07-13T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Price bridge & implementation acceptance

Thanks Maria — and great questions. I pulled a quick worked example and uploaded a short pricing table to the Drive link (see side-link). To be explicit on the items you asked for:

1) Effective rate calc: example shows incumbent invoice (monthly token columns) converted to equivalent Redwood per-token and per-request line items, with assumptions called out (sequence length, embed calls excluded). We’ll put the spreadsheet into the SOW as an appendix.

2) Credit handling: the onboarding credit will be issued as a dollar credit applied to invoices #1 and #2 (not refundable). We can split 70/30 across the two invoices if that helps cashflow.

3) Acceptance tests (deliverables):
   - Latency p95 & p99 under a staged load (test harness attached)
   - End-to-end inference throughput at declared concurrency levels
   - KV cache behavior: cold-start and steady-state under production-like prefix reuse
   - Error rate and functional correctness checks for a 72-hour rolling window

Escalation path: first contact is our infra lead Irene Choi (irene_choi@redwood.com), then me, then on-call eng. We’ll commit to a 48-hour remediation SLT after any failing acceptance test to triage and propose mitigation.

On timeline: July 28 works for our team — we’ll move kickoff to July 28 and update the SOW draft. Jordan, I attached the draft redlines (redlines_v1.pdf) and an SOW workbook (sow-cloudbridge.xlsx) for your legal/ops folks.

Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Maria Gonzales <maria@cloudbridge.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Legal <legal@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-07-13T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Price bridge & implementation acceptance

Looks good — thanks team.

Maria: confirming the three bullets from Marissa are the items procurement needs and that July 28 kickoff is acceptable.

Next steps (short):
- Jordan to open HubSpot deal and attach the SOW + appendix (DEAL-2025-0437).
- Legal to review attached redlines_v1.pdf and suggest any contract edits by EOD Monday. (Cc: legal).
- Irene to own the acceptance test checklist and share the test harness link + runbook by July 18.
- Jordan/Marissa: deliver the pricing worked example and finalize invoice split for onboarding credit by July 17.

If we get alignment on those points this afternoon we’ll route the SOW to CloudBridge for signature and target the July 28 kickoff.

Thanks — Jordan
